name: Even When You Know
tagline: You don't win arguments. You change what people see.
epigraph: The darkest band is on top. The clear one underneath is the heaviest.
glassware: a small stemmed pousse-café or cordial glass (about 75 ml), narrow and flared; no ice
language_row: Wren's Resonance (v2) and 4-gram pass on whoYouAre and yours: clean except "white crème de cacao" (an ingredient name); "it was for them" (*lover-caregiver*) rewritten; "plain view" (*regular-guy-hero*) unused; the closing line moved off "tell … why" (*On Their Behalf*, *regular-guy-ruler*). "I" only; no guest pronouns, archetype names or magic words; never "yours" for the drink. Lint 0 errors, 0 warnings. ✓

names_note: *Even When You Know* (Wren, Hester; 2–1). Tomás held *Heavier Than It Looks* (the clear bottom layer is the heaviest thing in the glass) and could take the pick. Also considered: *See for Yourself* (too near *Plain to See*), *Right Way Up*. Registry checked: no clash.
open_items: **For Robin (allergen table, not changed):** `creme_de_cacao_white` is `[]`, while Tomás's `cacao_nib_tincture_gin` row (explorer-magician) is `nuts, dairy` for shared-plant warnings; the two can't both be the safe side. Tomás recommends leaving crème de cacao at `[]` (on the page it's a cacao redistillate plus sugar, Oxford pdf 596); if Robin moves it, this pour loses veto-free. No label could be checked (web budget spent). New row `bourbon_beet` (contains none) and Tomás's layer densities (~1.12 / ~1.02 / ~0.945) are unsourced estimates; the method has a test step for new bottles. Balance is freeform (a layered drink; no *Codex* root), justified layer by layer in Checks. Nick's bar has no date on the page; the 1972 shaking answer is Le Mistral's proprietor's, relayed by Amy Vanderbilt. Lint warns of a motif overlap with *hero-magician* (white crème de cacao); Tomás accepted it in r4 with a reason (r4-tomas-3), and noted the shared "clear as water" wording for Robin.
